title: Polymeric Microneedle Array Fabrication by Photolithography
protocol: Clean a 4" glass wafer with piranha solution in a quartz tank for 20 min at 120 °C.
Deposit a layer of Chromium/Gold (30 nm Cr/1 µm Au) on the glass wafer using an e-beam evaporator once vacuum reaches 5 x 10^-6 Torr.
Pre-clean each material for 30 sec using the e-beam gun with shutter off to avoid deposition on wafers.
Apply a 2 μm thick photoresist by spinning 5 ml of solution at 3,000 rpm for 30 sec using a spin-spray coater system.
Prebake the photoresist on a hotplate at 100 °C for 1.5 min.
Expose and hard bake the photoresist at 120 °C for 30 min on a hot plate.
Pattern the Cr/Au layer using Cr and Au etchants through the photoresist mask.
Temporarily bond the glass wafer to a dummy silicon wafer for protection of un-patterned surface.
Place the glass wafer on a hot plate at 110 °C and melt wax on the opposite side to cover entire surface with wax.
Place a dummy silicon wafer in contact with the glass wafer.
Press to remove excess wax.
Place a clean room tissue paper on the hotplate to avoid spilling of the wax.
Mix hydrofluoric acid (49% v/v) and hydrochloric acid (37% v/v) solution in a volumetric ratio of 10:1 with a magnetic stirrer for isotropic etching.
Etch the lens using an optimized HF/HCl solution at a rate of 7 µm/min for 8.5 min.
Use a total volume of 200 ml of etching solution during the process.
Perform etching in a plastic container and take safety precautions.
Clean the wafer by rinsing with deionized (DI) water and drying it at room temperature.
Separate the glass wafer from the dummy silicon wafer after warming up the wax on a hot plate at 100 °C for 15 seconds.
Detach the glass wafer from the dummy silicon wafer as the wax melts.
Remove remaining wax, photoresist, and overhanging Cr/Au layers using ultrasonication with N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone solvent at 80 °C for 1 hour in an ultrasonic tank.
Create a PDMS mold replica of the microlenses fabricated on photomasks.
Characterize photomask dimensions (length and width) using a scanning electron microscope.
Characterize microlens PDMS mold replicas (depth and diameter) using a stereomicroscope.
Create a cavity of 2.5 cm × 0.9 cm using glass slides mounted on either side of a glass.
Determine the height of the cavity by stacking glass slides on either side.
Apply a thin layer of prepolymer solution containing Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA, MW = 258 Da) with 0.5% w/w 2-hydroxy-2-methyl-propiophenone (HMP) onto the glass slide.
Irradiate the setup with high intensity ultraviolet (UV) light for 2 sec.
Position the photomask with Cr/Au coated surfaces facing the interior of the cavity.
Ensure that the sides of the cavity walls do not obscure the lenses embedded in the photomask.
Fill the cavity with prepolymer solution until the Cr/Au coated surface is in contact with the solution without any visible bubbles.
Irradiate the setup with high intensity UV light for 1 sec at a distance of 3.5 cm from the UV source using the UV curing station with a UV filter range of 320-500 nm.
Use a collimating adaptor with the UV light probe.
Measure the intensity of UV light used using a radiometer.
Remove the photomask after UV exposure.
Pour the excess prepolymer solution that is not polymerized back into its original container for reuse.
Quantify the length and tip diameter of the MNs using a stereomicroscope according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Place the MNs attached onto the photomask in a well of a 24-well plate.
Add 300 - 400 µl of prepolymer solution into the well until the needles are submerged to a desired height.
Irradiate the setup with high intensity UV light (15.1 W/cm²) from a distance of 10.5 cm for 1 sec.
Separate the backing layer on the MN array from the photomask using a sharp blade.
Quantify the length, tip diameter and base diameter of the MNs with the backing layer using a stereomicroscope according to manufacturer’s instructions.
